messages:
incidents-bot: PAGE: sev2 — Elevated gateway 5xx/timeouts for Private VPC egress (multiple customers). Triggered 1716004300. Affected: private egress -> external model provider. Threshold: 5xx > 3% over 5m. Runbook: <https://redwood.internal/runbooks/vpc-egress>|vpc-egress-runbook. Please ack and triage.

sylvia (oncall): Acked. I'm looking at dashboards now — latency and 504 spikes from our egress gateways. Is this limited to a single AZ?

maria-sre: Not single AZ — metric shards show elevated 502/504 across gw-prod-*/egress in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Kernel conntrack and NAT metrics spiking on gw-prod-3.

sylvia (oncall): @liam-netinfra can you check peering route/state and any recent security-group or firewall policy changes? I see a Terraform apply in infra-ci ~ 1716002000 but not sure if it's related.

liam-netinfra: Looking. I see a recent security-group rule change — outbound deny for ephemeral range 32768-61000 was added to a shared egress SG in the infra account (change set id: cs-8823). That would break SNAT reuse if clients rely on ephemeral ports. Rolling back check in progress.

support-lead: Do we have customer impact list? Which tenants are hitting failures?

maria-sre: Support logs show three customers with elevated 5xx: acme-corp, storylabs, and partner-ml. Their requests hit the same egress pool (gw-prod-3). Error samples: HTTP 504 gateway timeout, upstream connection reset. Sample curl from gw: `curl -v https://api.vendor/model  --max-time 10` -> connection reset after SYN.

sylvia (oncall): Ok, if outbound ephemeral ports were restricted that explains connection churn -> NAT port exhaustion and then 504s. Maria, can you confirm conntrack and NAT table utilization?

maria-sre: conntrack_count: 1.9M (limit 2M); NAT ports in use: 98% across gw-prod-3; conntrack TIME_WAIT backlog high. Attaching quick tcpdump extract below.

maria-sre: ```
# tcpdump -n -i eth0 'tcp and host 1.2.3.4'
20:10:21.123456 IP 10.0.12.34.56789 > 34.56.78.90.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240, options [mss 1460], length 0
20:10:21.223456 IP 10.0.12.34.56789 > 34.56.78.90.443: Flags [S], ack 0
# repeated SYNs, many SYN retransmits
```

sylvia (oncall): Good evidence. Liam, can you roll back the SG change? If it's in infra CI, we need to revert and reapply. If rollback takes time, can we open a temporary NAT pool or rotate egress pool to another subnet?

liam-netinfra: Rolling back CS-8823 now. Also creating a temporary secondary NAT gateway with larger ephemeral allocation and adding gw-prod-5 as alternate egress. ETA ~ 12m. Command I'm running: `terraform apply -target=module.egress.security_group_rule.cs-8823 -destroy` (dry-run succeeded).

deploy-bot: deploy job started by liam-netinfra at 1716004900 for infra-ci. Job id: deploy-48219. No dependent services impacted.

maria-sre: After starting rollback, NAT port utilization dropped to 72% on gw-prod-3 within ~3m; conntrack count falling. Error rate dropped from 6.1% -> 1.2% over 5m.

sylvia (oncall): Nice. Notify support and customers. @support-lead please post an update to affected tenants: brief root cause (egress SG restricting ephemeral ports), mitigation (rolled back SG, provisioning temporary NAT pool), ETA for full verification (30m).

support-lead: On it. Drafting customer message now. Will include workaround note to retry in a few minutes and that we're monitoring.

maria-sre: One follow-up: we saw a spike in connections from an internal batch job that opened many short-lived outbound connections at ~1716001800. That coincided with the SG change and caused quicker exhaustion. Recommend we throttle that job and add better egress connection pooling in the app.

sylvia (oncall): Add a post-incident action item for rate-limiting that batch job and for test coverage on infra CI changes that touch shared egress SGs.

liam-netinfra: Rolling NAT pool and SG rollback complete. Running smoke tests to vendor endpoints. Smoke: 200 OK for 10 consecutive requests.

maria-sre: Error rate steady at 0.6% over last 10m, within normal bounds. No further 5xx alerts for these customers.

sylvia (oncall): Preparing incident summary for a quick postmortem: Cause = infra CI security-group rule inadvertently blocked ephemeral outbound ports for shared egress SG, combined with an internal spike in short-lived outbound connections -> NAT port/conntrack exhaustion -> 504/502 observed by customers. Mitigation = rollback SG rule, provision temporary NAT pool, throttle offending batch job.

sylvia (oncall): I'm handing off to jordan (next oncall) for continued monitoring and follow-ups. Jordan, prioritize: 1) verify long-term NAT capacity plan, 2) coordinate with infra CI to add safeguards, 3) confirm customer comms. Handoff time 1716020000.

jordan (next-oncall): Acked. Will take it from here. I'll post a follow-up once we have RCA and action items written.

incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: sev2 downgraded to monitoring at 1716021200. No active paging for this thread.

sylvia (oncall): Thanks all. Adding P0->P1 ticket in backlog for automated infra CI preflight checks for shared SG changes.

support-lead: Customers notified at 1716021300. Responses are positive. Closing customer-impact window at 1716021400 unless something else pops up.

maria-sre: Note for postmortem: consider conntrack tuning and ephemeral port ranges for NAT on reserve pools. Also add metrics alert for conntrack % utilization so we don't climb to 95% without immediate paging.

liam-netinfra: I'll file infra change to prevent outbound-deny on shared egress SGs without explicit owner approval.

sylvia (oncall): Closing thread handoff. Good job everyone :thumbsup:
